methodological_rigor.justification: Robust observational study combining bulk RNA-seq (162 resected stage I LUAD tumors) with spatial transcriptomics validation. VI-associated gene signature derived and validated in independent cohort. Pre-surgical biopsy cohort demonstrates biomarker detectability in limited tissue. Multiregional sampling robustness assessed. However: no sample size calculation for signature derivation, validation cohort size/characteristics not detailed in abstract, cutoff determination methodology unspecified.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Vascular invasion (VI) predicts recurrence and surgical benefit in stage I LUAD. Preoperative biomarker enabling VI prediction directly informs treatment decisions (lobectomy vs wedge resection, adjuvant therapy). High clinical utility in early-stage lung cancer management.

reporting_quality.justification: Study design clearly describes bulk RNA-seq (162 tumors), spatial transcriptomics validation subset, pre-surgical biopsy cohort, and multiregional sampling robustness testing. Gene expression methodology (alignment, normalization) likely detailed. Missing: detailed baseline characteristics, explicit cutoff derivation and validation methodology, cross-validation approach specification.

novelty_literature.justification: VI-associated transcriptional signature is novel for stage I LUAD. Extends prior VI biology literature by identifying reproducible gene expression program detectable beyond invasive focus. Biomarker application is clinically novel; mechanistic pathway insights limited.

writing_presentation.justification: Study design and biomarker development pathway logically presented. Abstract clearly articulates VI clinical significance, transcriptional program identification, validation strategy, and preoperative applicability. Methods structure appropriate for complex biomarker study.

key_strengths: Novel identification of VI-associated gene expression program reproducibly detectable beyond invasive focus across 162 resected tumors
Biomarker validation in independent cohort demonstrating predictive value for VI status and recurrence in stage I LUAD
Spatial transcriptomics confirms signatures localize beyond invasive focus, supporting distant detection in limited biopsies
Robustness assessment via multiregional sampling shows marker stability despite intra-tumor heterogeneity
key_concerns: Sample sizes and cross-validation approach not detailed in abstract; risk of overfit to derivation cohort
Cutoff determination methodology for biomarker classification not specified
Pre-surgical biopsy cohort likely limited in size; may not represent full spectrum of VI-positive/negative cases
Mechanistic insights into VI biology limited; biomarker is correlative rather than mechanistic
No external validation in independent institution cohort; generalizability to other centers unclear
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically valuable biomarker with solid validation strategy. Tier 3 appropriate pending independent external validation.
